page.title: Court Costs Calculator
page.description: Choose the amount in dispute (the value of the claim), the type of case and the level of court to calculate the stamp fee for a complaint, appeal or final appeal (with the 10% e-litigation discount) and the service fees to pay in advance.
page.lead: Calculates the money you pay to the court when you start a lawsuit (the stamp fee and service fees). You can choose a civil lawsuit, a payment order, conciliation, or a family case such as divorce.
page.notice: This is a reference amount that covers only the costs you first pay to the court. It does not include lawyer's fees, appraisal fees or witness costs, and the amount changes if claims are combined or changed. The actual amount is set by the court where you file, so talk to a lawyer before filing a lawsuit.

ui.soga: Amount in dispute (value of the claim)
ui.sogaHint: For a money claim, the amount in dispute is usually the principal you are claiming. Do not include interest or damages for late payment.
ui.appellees: Number of opposing parties (appellees or respondents in the final appeal)
ui.floorNote: rounded down to the nearest KRW 100
ui.note: The stamp fee is the fee attached to a complaint or application. The service fee is postage paid in advance so that the court can send documents ({unit} per service). Any service fee left over is returned when the case ends. The amount can differ if you file several claims together or there are many opposing parties, and the actual amount is set by the court where you file.

errors.soga: Enter the amount in dispute (value of the claim).

kinds.family-fixed: Divorce and similar family litigation (Class A/B)
kinds.family-damages: Family litigation for damages, such as for emotional distress (Class C)

hints.civil: A first-instance case with an amount in dispute of {limit} or less is treated as a small claims case when calculating service fees.
hints.payment-order: A simple procedure in which the court orders the other party to pay. If the other party objects, the case moves to a lawsuit.
hints.mediation: A procedure for reaching an agreement before a judge or a conciliation commissioner.
hints.family-fixed: Family litigation in which the claim is not measured by an amount of money, such as a judicial divorce or nullity of marriage. The stamp fee is a fixed amount.
hints.family-damages: Family litigation claiming money, such as damages for emotional distress caused by a divorce. The rate is half the civil rate.
hints.family-division: When property division is claimed on its own. The amount in dispute is the amount you claim.

cases.civilSmall: Civil small claims case, first instance
cases.civilFirst: Civil case before a single judge or panel, first instance

steps.familyFixed: Family litigation flat fee (paper filing basis)
steps.finalElec: Final appeal (2 times) with e-litigation discount
